correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly fixes real independent Gaussian sketches, reduces arbitrary rectangular matrices using SVD, computes energy-term variances, verifies Lyapunov fourth-moment decay under the stated effective-rank hypothesis, applies a continuous chi-square law at the zero threshold and uniform integrability to clipping. Gamma size-bias identities give exact bias, and constrained rate-function minimization establishes a unique rank-one saddle at u=v=2 with its curvature and leading prefactor. The 2026 primary variance formula is independently reconstructed and credited. Computations in verify.py check finite algebra, gamma constants and seeded experiments, not infinite limits.

value.rationale: For a strictly positive squared Frobenius norm, an unweighted two-sided estimator with one independent Gaussian probe per side has asymptotically 15.73% negative output frequency even along sequences of matrices of diverging effective rank. Positivity clipping creates 25.78% asymptotic relative upward bias, directly affecting log-based or positivity-constrained downstream uses. The rank-one and spectrally flat sketch-budget negative tails have different exponents, producing a nontrivial and natural spectral robustness classification beyond a variance bound. No generalization to weighted Hutch# or other sketches is claimed.
